s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on the trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on the lower lip with sparing of the surrounding skin
key_facts: Female patient in her early 40s
No other medical history
Topical corticosteroids did not control symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Normal urine porphyrin analysis
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis, erosions, and nodular lymphocyte infiltrate
Phototest with solar simulator showed delayed erythema to UV-A

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Delayed erythema to UV-A on phototest

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and erythematous papules

shortlist.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and scales on the lower lip

shortlist.label: Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphoid infiltrate in the dermis and erythematous papules

shortlist.label: Cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and germinal centers in the dermis

raw.rationale: The presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center, along with the clinical presentation of erythematous papules and the lack of response to topical corticosteroids, supports this diagnosis. The delayed erythema to UV-A on phototest also aligns with Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate, which can be photosensitive.

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While the patient had a delayed reaction to UV-A, the skin biopsy findings and the specific pattern of lymphocyte infiltrate are more characteristic of Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more necrotic and ulcerative lesions, which were not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
rejected.why: The biopsy findings and the clinical presentation do not fully align with the typical features of pityriasis lichenoides chronica, such as the presence of a wedge-shaped lymphocytic infiltrate.

rejected.label: Cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia
rejected.why: While this condition can present with similar biopsy findings, the clinical context and the specific pattern of lymphocyte infiltrate are more suggestive of Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate.
